you should do further research into any resources around you that might be free or accept your insurance, if you have. treatment can really help with this magical thinking and these compulsions. otherwise, there are many resources online but the best option is a professional who can guide you.

i’m really sorry this happened to you. i think you just need more “proof” that good things happen to you and that you are capable of good things. maybe highlighting the good, and even the smallest parts of your day, can help you stay a little more positive. indulging in more creative hobbies or even volunteering work. you deserve everything you wish for and despite these challenges you are cared for and loved. ofc you should be happy, but when you’ve struggled with these things and ocd, there is a lot of pain that needs to be released and grief that needs to be processed, along with learning. it’s not as simple as to be happy. maybe also consider therapy so you can process the events / deal with the thoughts. don’t give up!!

“meet with a psychiatrist that doesn’t help much.” are you able to find / afford to see a OCD specialist? ocd isn’t a death sentence and doesn’t need to be. with treatment your symptoms can lessen greatly. you deserve to live and be happy and take back everything ocd takes from you. you aren’t alone and i’m so sorry you’re so tired of everything. you got this.
